title.zh: 卷四十一 志第二十二: 儀衞上 常朝儀衛內外立仗、常行儀衛行仗 法駕黃麾仗
title.en: Volume 41 Treatises 22: Ceremonial Guards 1 - Inner and Outer Armed Guards of Honor in Regular Court Assemblies; Marching Armed Guards; Armed Imperial Command Carriage
title.raw: 卷四十一 志第二十二: 儀衞上 常朝儀衛內外立仗、常行儀衛行仗 法駕黃麾仗 Volume 41 Treatises 22: Ceremonial Guards 1 - Inner and Outer Armed Guards of Honor in Regular Court Assemblies; Marching Armed Guards; Armed Imperial Command Carriage

sentences.zh: 常朝儀衛內外立仗、常行儀衛行仗

translations.literal: Regular court ceremonial escort, inner and outer standing armed guards; regular processional ceremonial escort, marching armed guards
translations.idiomatic: Inner and Outer Standing Guards for Regular Court Ceremonial Escort; Marching Guards for Regular Processional Ceremonial Escort

sentences.zh: 金制，天子之儀衛，一曰立仗，二曰行仗。

translations.literal: Under Jin regulations, the Son of Heaven's ceremonial guard had two types: first, standing armed guards; second, marching armed guards.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin institutional practice, the emperor's ceremonial guard was divided into standing formations and marching formations.

sentences.zh: 其衛士，曰護衛、曰親軍、曰弩手，曰控鶴、曰傘子、曰長行。

translations.literal: Its guardsmen were called bodyguards, personal guards, crossbowmen, crane handlers, umbrella bearers, and long-march guards.
translations.idiomatic: The personnel included bodyguards, imperial guard troops, crossbowmen, crane handlers, umbrella bearers, and long-march escorts.

sentences.zh: 立仗則有殿庭內仗、殿庭外仗，凡大禮、大朝會則用之。

translations.literal: For standing armed guards there were inner and outer hall-court formations, used for all major rites and major court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: Standing formations comprised inner and outer hall-court deployments, employed at major rites and grand court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 其朔望常朝，弩手百人分立兩階而已。

translations.literal: For the new- and full-moon regular audiences, only a hundred crossbowmen stood divided on the two flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: At the regular new- and full-moon audiences, only a hundred crossbowmen were posted on the two stairways.

sentences.zh: 行仗則有法駕、大駕、黃麾仗，凡行幸及郊廟祀享則用之。

translations.literal: For marching armed guards there were the imperial command carriage formation, the grand carriage formation, and the yellow-banner formation, used whenever the emperor traveled and for suburban and temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Marching formations included the imperial command carriage guard, the grand carriage guard, and the yellow-banner guard, used when the emperor went on progress or performed suburban and temple sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 其非大禮遠出，則有常行儀衛、宮中導從焉。

translations.literal: When it was not a major rite or a distant journey, there were the regular processional ceremonial escort and palace interior guides and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: For occasions that were not major rites or distant travel, there were the regular processional guard and palace escorts.

sentences.zh: 大抵模仿宋制，錯綜增損而用之。

translations.literal: For the most part they imitated Song regulations, adapting and adding or subtracting as they applied them.
translations.idiomatic: In general they followed Song practice, selectively adapting and revising it as needed.

sentences.zh: 其宿衛則見《兵志》云。

translations.literal: Palace night guards are discussed in the Military Treatises.
translations.idiomatic: Palace night guard duty is treated in the Military Treatises.

sentences.zh: 初，國制，凡朔望常朝日，殿下列衛士，簾下置甲兵。

translations.literal: At first, under national regulations, on every new- and full-moon regular audience day, guardsmen were arrayed below the hall and armored troops were placed under the curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, under the dynasty's original rules, on each new- and full-moon audience day guards were posted below the hall and armored troops stationed behind the curtains.

sentences.zh: 正隆元年，海陵去甲兵，惟存錦衣弩手百人，分立兩階。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenglong, Hailing removed the armored troops, retaining only a hundred brocade-clad crossbowmen standing divided on the two flights of steps.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenglong (1156), Emperor Hailing removed the armored troops and kept only a hundred brocade-clad crossbowmen, posted on the two stairways.

sentences.zh: 其儀，都副點檢，公服偏帶。

translations.literal: For the ritual dress, the chief and deputy inspectors wore official robes with side sashes.
translations.idiomatic: The prescribed attire for the chief and deputy inspectors was official court dress with a side-worn belt.

sentences.zh: 常朝則展紫。

translations.literal: For regular audiences they wore spread purple.
translations.idiomatic: At regular audiences they wore open purple robes.

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍、宿直將軍，展紫，金束帶，各執玉、水晶及金飾骨朵。

translations.literal: The left and right guard generals and night-duty generals wore spread purple, gold belts, and each held jade, crystal, or gold-mounted maces.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right guard generals and rotating-duty generals wore open purple with gold belts, each carrying a jade, crystal, or gold-mounted mace.

sentences.zh: 左右親衛，盤裹紫襖，塗金束帶，骨朵，佩兵械。

translations.literal: The left and right personal guards wore wrapped purple jackets, gilded belts, maces, and carried weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right personal guards wore wrapped purple jackets, gilded belts, and maces, with arms at their belts.

sentences.zh: 供禦弩手、傘子百人，並金花交腳襆頭，塗金銅鈒襯花束帶，骨朵。

translations.literal: A hundred imperial crossbowmen and umbrella bearers all wore gold-flowered cross-foot turbans, gilded copper-inlaid floral belts, and maces.
translations.idiomatic: The hundred imperial crossbowmen and umbrella bearers all wore gold-flowered crossed-foot turbans, gilded copper-inlaid floral belts, and maces.

sentences.zh: 左右班執儀物內侍二十人，展紫，塗金束帶。

translations.literal: Twenty inner attendants of the left and right shifts holding ritual implements wore spread purple and gilded belts.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty inner attendants from the left and right shifts, bearing ritual implements, wore open purple and gilded belts.

sentences.zh: 朝參日，弩手、傘子直於殿門外，分兩面排立。

translations.literal: On audience days crossbowmen and umbrella bearers stood sentry outside the hall gate, arrayed in two facing lines.
translations.idiomatic: On days of audience the crossbowmen and umbrella bearers stood guard outside the hall gate in two facing ranks.

sentences.zh: 司辰報時畢，皇帝御殿坐，鳴鞭，閣門報班齊。

translations.literal: When the time-keeper finished announcing the hour, the emperor took his seat in the hall, the whip was sounded, and the gate officers reported that the ranks were complete.
translations.idiomatic: After the timekeeper announced the hour, the emperor took the throne, the whip was sounded, and the gate officers reported that all ranks were in place.

sentences.zh: 執擎儀物內侍分降殿階，南向立。

translations.literal: Inner attendants holding ritual implements descended the hall steps in turn and stood facing south.
translations.idiomatic: The inner attendants bearing ritual implements came down the hall steps in succession and stood facing south.

sentences.zh: 點檢司起居，弩手、傘子於殿門外北面山呼聲喏，訖，即於殿門外東西相向排立。

translations.literal: The inspection office reported the emperor's wellbeing; crossbowmen and umbrella bearers outside the hall gate shouted their acclamation facing north; when finished they arrayed facing one another east and west outside the hall gate.
translations.idiomatic: The inspection office reported the emperor's wellbeing; crossbowmen and umbrella bearers outside the hall gate cried their acclamation to the north; when done they formed facing ranks east and west outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 都點檢以次三員升殿，都點檢在東近南，左副又少南，右副在西，東向對立。

translations.literal: The chief inspector and the next two officers in order ascended the hall; the chief inspector was in the east near the south, the left deputy somewhat further south, the right deputy in the west, all facing east and standing opposite one another.
translations.idiomatic: The chief inspector and two deputies in order of precedence ascended the hall: the chief inspector east and near the south, the left deputy a little farther south, the right deputy in the west—all facing east and standing opposite one another.

sentences.zh: 左右衛將軍在殿下東西對立。

translations.literal: The left and right guard generals stood opposite one another east and west below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The left and right guard generals stood facing each other east and west below the hall.

sentences.zh: 省臣隨班起居畢，左右司侍郎從宰執奏事。

translations.literal: When provincial ministers had finished greeting according to rank, the left and right secretariat vice ministers followed the chief ministers in presenting business.
translations.idiomatic: After the provincial ministers had completed their greetings in rank order, the left and right secretariat vice ministers joined the chief ministers in presenting memorials.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史隨班起居畢，東西對立于左右衛將軍之北，少前。

translations.literal: When the palace censors had finished greeting according to rank, they stood opposite one another east and west north of the left and right guard generals, slightly forward.
translations.idiomatic: After the palace censors had completed their greetings, they stood facing each other east and west, north of the guard generals and slightly forward.

sentences.zh: 修起居注分殿陛東西對立於殿欄外副階下，以俟。

translations.literal: Recorders of imperial activity stood opposite one another east and west at the secondary steps outside the hall balustrade, waiting.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial diarists stood facing each other east and west on the secondary steps outside the hall balustrade, waiting their turn.

sentences.zh: 奏事畢，皇帝還閣，侍衛者乃退。

translations.literal: When presentations were finished the emperor returned to the private chambers and only then did the guards withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When business was concluded the emperor withdrew to the inner chambers, and only then did the escort withdraw.

sentences.zh: 凡遇大禮、大朝會，則有內外立仗。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a major rite or major court assembly, there were inner and outer standing armed guards.
translations.idiomatic: At major rites and grand court assemblies there were inner and outer standing formations.

sentences.zh: 熙宗皇統元年正月，上冊寶，立仗一千一百八十人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Huangtong under Emperor Xizong, at the presentation of the seals and credentials, standing armed guards numbered 1,180 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Huangtong 1 (1141), when Emperor Xizong received the seals and jade insignia, the standing guard numbered 1,180 men.

sentences.zh: 自是以後，至海陵時，俱用三千人。

translations.literal: From then on until the time of Hailing, all used three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: From that time until Emperor Hailing's reign the formation regularly employed three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定七年，上冊寶，頗損其數，且以天德、貞元不設車輅，遂並去之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dading under Emperor Shizong, at the presentation of the seals and credentials, the number was considerably reduced, and because carriage equipage had not been provided under Tiande and Zhenyuan, that too was entirely removed.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 7 (1167), when Emperor Shizong received the seals and jade insignia, the guard was sharply reduced; because no carriage equipage had been used under Tiande and Zhenyuan, that element was dropped entirely.

sentences.zh: 是後，或減至二千，或一千、或八百、或六百人。

translations.literal: Thereafter the number was sometimes reduced to two thousand, or one thousand, or eight hundred, or six hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: After that it was sometimes cut to two thousand, or one thousand, eight hundred, or six hundred men.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，海陵立後，發冊勤政殿，設黃麾細仗，用前六部，攝官七十一，擎執六百七十八人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, when Hailing installed his empress, the credentials were issued at the Diligence in Government Hall with yellow-banner reduced armed guard using the front six sections, 71 acting officers, and 678 bearers.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2 (1150), when Emperor Hailing installed his empress, the patent was issued at the Diligence in Government Hall with a reduced yellow-banner guard: the front six sections, 71 acting officers, and 678 bearers.

sentences.zh: 受冊泰和殿，用後六部，攝官三十六，擎執三百二十二人。

translations.literal: Receiving the credentials at the Grand Harmony Hall used the rear six sections, 36 acting officers, and 322 bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the patent at the Grand Harmony Hall used the rear six sections, with 36 acting officers and 322 bearers.

sentences.zh: 大定八年正月，冊皇太子于大安殿，用黃麾半仗二千二百六十五人，奉表于仁政殿用黃麾細仗一千四百二人。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year of Dading the heir apparent was enfeoffed at the Great Peace Hall using half yellow-banner armed guard of 2,265 men; presenting the memorial at the Benevolent Government Hall used reduced yellow-banner armed guard of 1,402 men.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dading 8 the heir apparent was installed at the Great Peace Hall with a half yellow-banner guard of 2,265 men; presenting the memorial at the Benevolent Government Hall used a reduced yellow-banner guard of 1,402 men.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，冊皇太孫，亦如之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year the heir presumptive was enfeoffed in the same manner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year the imperial great-grandson was installed in the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 大定八年，黃麾半仗，攝官一百七十五人，擎執二千八十一人，編排職掌九人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dading, half yellow-banner armed guard had 175 acting officers, 2,081 bearers, and 9 men in charge of arrangement duties.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 8 a half yellow-banner guard comprised 175 acting officers, 2,081 bearers, and 9 arrangement officers.

sentences.zh: 殿庭內仗。

translations.literal: Inner hall-court armed guard.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Hall-Court Formation

sentences.zh: 以中心東西相向一重，並面北旗幟為中道。

translations.literal: A single rank facing one another east and west at the center, with banners facing north forming the central path.
translations.idiomatic: A single rank faced each other east and west at the center, with north-facing banners marking the central aisle.

sentences.zh: 左行，自北西向排列。

translations.literal: The left row, arranged from the north facing west.
translations.idiomatic: The left row was arrayed from the north, facing west.

sentences.zh: 黃麾幡一首，執者三人。

translations.literal: One yellow-banner pennant, three bearers.
translations.idiomatic: One yellow-banner pennant, borne by three men.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，大雉扇二。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, two large ritual fans.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk, two large pheasant-tail fans.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，中雉扇六，碧襴官一，小雉扇六。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, six medium ritual fans; one officer in green patterned silk, six small ritual fans.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and six medium pheasant-tail fans; one officer in green patterned silk and six small pheasant-tail fans.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，硃團扇六。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, six vermilion round fans.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and six vermilion round fans.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，睥睨四。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, four battlements-shaped parasols.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and four battlement-shaped parasols.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，紅大傘一。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, one large red umbrella.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and one large red umbrella.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，紫方傘二。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, two purple square umbrellas.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and two purple square umbrellas.

sentences.zh: 碧襴官一，華蓋一。

translations.literal: One officer in green patterned silk, one ceremonial canopy.
translations.idiomatic: One officer in green patterned silk and one ceremonial canopy.

sentences.zh: 右行，東向列者，並同。

translations.literal: The right row, arrayed facing east, was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The right row, arrayed facing east, matched this arrangement.

sentences.zh: 面北，第一行，牙門旗八，共二十四人，分左右。

translations.literal: Facing north, the first row: eight gate pennants, twenty-four men in all, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Facing north, first row: eight gate pennants, twenty-four men total, split left and right.

sentences.zh: 留中道。

translations.literal: Leaving the central path clear.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the central aisle open.

sentences.zh: 第二行，監門校尉十二，分左右。

translations.literal: Second row: twelve gate-guard commandants, divided left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: twelve gate-guard commandants, left and right.

sentences.zh: 第三行，長壽幢一，押旗大將軍一，居中，次東五方龍旗十五，次西五方鳳旗十五。

translations.literal: Third row: one longevity banner, one general escorting the flags at the center; next to the east fifteen five-direction dragon flags; next to the west fifteen five-direction phoenix flags.
translations.idiomatic: Third row: one longevity banner and one flag-escort general at the center; then fifteen five-direction dragon flags to the east and fifteen five-direction phoenix flags to the west.

sentences.zh: 第四行，自內而東，青龍旗五，紅龍旗二十。

translations.literal: Fourth row, from within toward the east: five azure dragon flags, twenty red dragon flags.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth row, from the center eastward: five azure dragon flags and twenty red dragon flags.

sentences.zh: 自內而西，青龍旗五，紅龍旗二十。

translations.literal: From within toward the west: five azure dragon flags, twenty red dragon flags.
translations.idiomatic: From the center westward: five azure dragon flags and twenty red dragon flags.

sentences.zh: 第五行，同上，又君王萬歲旗一，五人居中。

translations.literal: Fifth row, as above; also one "Myriad Years to the Sovereign" flag, five men at the center.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth row, as above, plus one "Long Live the Sovereign" flag with five men at the center.

sentences.zh: 日旗一，五人在左。

translations.literal: One sun flag, five men on the left.
translations.idiomatic: One sun flag, five men to the left.

sentences.zh: 月旗一，五人在右。

translations.literal: One moon flag, five men on the right.
translations.idiomatic: One moon flag, five men to the right.

sentences.zh: 第六行，自內而東，天下太平旗、苣紋旗、日月合璧旗、苣紋旗、青龍旗、赤龍旗、河瀆旗、江瀆旗各一，旗五人，排仗通直官一，排仗大將一。

translations.literal: Sixth row, from within toward the east: one each of the All Under Heaven at Peace flag, artemisia-pattern flag, sun-and-moon conjoined flag, artemisia-pattern flag, azure dragon flag, red dragon flag, Yellow River stream flag, and Yangtze River stream flag—five men per flag; one formation direct officer and one formation general.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth row, from the center eastward: one each of the All Under Heaven at Peace, artemisia-pattern, sun-and-moon conjoined, artemisia-pattern, azure dragon, red dragon, Yellow River stream, and Yangtze River stream flags—five men per flag—plus one formation direct officer and one formation general.

sentences.zh: 未、午、巳、辰、卯、寅旗各一，青天王旗、白天王旗各一。

translations.literal: One each of the wei, wu, si, chen, mao, and yin branch flags; one each of the azure celestial king flag and white celestial king flag.
translations.idiomatic: One flag each for the wei, wu, si, chen, mao, and yin earthly branches, and one each for the azure and white celestial king flags.

sentences.zh: 自內而西，祥雲旗、五星連珠旗、祥雲旗、黃龍旗、白龍旗、黑龍旗、淮瀆旗、濟瀆旗各一，旗五人，通直官一，大將一。

translations.literal: From within toward the west: one each of the auspicious cloud flag, five stars in alignment flag, auspicious cloud flag, yellow dragon flag, white dragon flag, black dragon flag, Huai River stream flag, and Ji River stream flag—five men per flag; one direct officer and one general.
translations.idiomatic: From the center westward: one each of the auspicious cloud, five stars in alignment, auspicious cloud, yellow dragon, white dragon, black dragon, Huai River stream, and Ji River stream flags—five men per flag—plus one direct officer and one general.

sentences.zh: 申、酉、戌、亥、子、醜旗各一、緋天王旗、皁天王旗各一。

translations.literal: One each of the shen, you, xu, hai, zi, and chou branch flags; one each of the scarlet celestial king flag and black celestial king flag.
translations.idiomatic: One flag each for the shen, you, xu, hai, zi, and chou earthly branches, and one each for the scarlet and black celestial king flags.

sentences.zh: 第七行，自內而東，孔雀旗一，五人。

translations.literal: Seventh row, from within toward the east: one peacock flag, five men.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh row, from the center eastward: one peacock flag with five men.

sentences.zh: 蒼烏旗、兕旗、犛牛旗、騼䮷旗，赤熊旗、白狼旗、金鸚鵡旗、馴犀旗、角端旗、狖鸃旗、騶牙旗、野馬旗、瑞麥旗、甘露旗各一，旗五人。

translations.literal: One each of the azure bird flag, rhinoceros flag, yak flag, camelopard flag, red bear flag, white wolf flag, golden parrot flag, tame rhinoceros flag, horned tip flag, owl-parrot flag, zouya flag, wild horse flag, auspicious wheat flag, and sweet dew flag—five men per flag.
translations.idiomatic: One each of the azure bird, rhinoceros, yak, camelopard, red bear, white wolf, golden parrot, tame rhinoceros, horned tip, owl-parrot, zouya, wild horse, auspicious wheat, and sweet dew flags—five men per flag.

sentences.zh: 自內而西者同。

translations.literal: From within toward the west was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The arrangement from the center westward was the same.

sentences.zh: 外仗。

translations.literal: Outer armed guard.
translations.idiomatic: Outer Formation

sentences.zh: 在門外。

translations.literal: Outside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Posted outside the gate.

sentences.zh: 左邊，西向，自北排列。

translations.literal: On the left side, facing west, arrayed from the north.
translations.idiomatic: On the left, facing west, arrayed from the north.

sentences.zh: 第一部，第一行，侍御史、大將軍、折沖都尉各一，主帥三。

translations.literal: First section, first row: one attendant censor, one great general, and one assault-resistance commandant each; three section commanders.
translations.idiomatic: First section, first row: one attendant censor, one great general, and one assault-resistance commandant each, with three section commanders.

sentences.zh: 第二行，絳引幡五首十五人，龍頭竿四、弓矢五、揭鼓二、龍頭竿四、儀鍠斧五、龍頭竿四、硃刀盾五、龍頭竿四、綠刀盾五、龍頭竿四、小戟五。

translations.literal: Second row: five crimson guide pennants with fifteen men; four dragon-head poles, five bows and arrows, two signal drums, four dragon-head poles, five ceremonial gong-axes, four dragon-head poles, five vermilion blade-shields, four dragon-head poles, five green blade-shields, four dragon-head poles, five small halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Second row: five crimson guide pennants (fifteen men); then in sequence four dragon-head poles, five bows and arrows, two signal drums, four dragon-head poles, five ceremonial gong-axes, four dragon-head poles, five vermilion blade-shields, four dragon-head poles, five green blade-shields, four dragon-head poles, and five small halberds.

sentences.zh: 第三行，與第一行同。

translations.literal: Third row, the same as the first row.
translations.idiomatic: Third row, identical to the first.

sentences.zh: 第四行，與第二行同。

translations.literal: Fourth row, the same as the second row.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth row, identical to the second.

sentences.zh: 第二部、第三部、第四部、第五部以次而南，各為前後四行，其名數與第一部同，惟無絳引幡。

translations.literal: The second, third, fourth, and fifth sections continued south in order, each with four front-and-rear rows; their names and numbers were the same as the first section, except without crimson guide pennants.

sentences.zh: 弩手二百人，軍使五人，控鶴二百人，首領四人，俱服紅地藏根牡丹錦襖、金鳳花交腳襆頭、塗金銀束帶，控鶴或皁帽碧襖，各執金鍍銀蒜瓣骨朵。

translations.literal: Two hundred crossbowmen, five military envoys, and two hundred crane handlers with four leaders—all wore red peony brocade jackets with dark-ground roots, gold phoenix-flower crossed-foot turbans, and gilded silver belts; crane handlers sometimes wore black caps and green jackets, and all carried gilded silver garlic-clove maces.

All carried gilded silver garlic-clove maces.

sentences.zh: 長行四百人，拳腳襆頭、紅錦四䙆襖、塗金束帶，二人紫衫前導，無執物，餘執列糸骨朵七十八、瓜八十八，鐙三十四，在控鶴前，金吾仗八十、金花大劍六十俱垂紅絨結子、儀鍠斧五十八，在控鶴後。

translations.literal: Four hundred long-march guards in fist-and-foot turbans, red brocade four-panel jackets, and gilded belts: two in purple robes went ahead as guides without implements; the rest bore seventy-eight strung maces, eighty-eight melons, and thirty-four stirrups before the crane handlers; eighty Golden Guard maces, sixty gold-flower great swords all hung with red velvet knots, and fifty-eight ceremonial gong-axes followed behind the crane handlers.
translations.idiomatic: Four hundred long-march guards wore fist-and-foot turbans, red brocade four-panel jackets, and gilded belts. Two in purple robes led without implements; the rest carried seventy-eight strung maces, eighty-eight melons, and thirty-four stirrups ahead of the crane handlers, while eighty Golden Guard maces, sixty gold-flower great swords with red velvet knots, and fifty-eight ceremonial gong-axes marched behind them.

sentences.zh: 其常朝、御殿、郊廟、臨幸，凡步輦出入則有近侍導從，執金鍍銀骨朵者二人，左右扇十人，拂子四人，香盒二人，香球二人，節二人，幢二人，盂一人，唾壺一人，淨巾一人，鐁鑼一人，水罐一人，交椅一人，斧一人，皇帝出閣則分立閣門之外，導引至殿，皇帝升座則降階以俟，入閣然後放仗。

translations.literal: At regular audiences, imperial hall sessions, suburban and temple rites, and imperial visits, whenever the palanquin entered or left there were close attendants to guide and follow: two bearing gilded silver maces; ten fan bearers left and right; four whisk holders; two incense-box bearers; two incense-ball bearers; two tally bearers; two banner bearers; one bowl bearer; one spittoon bearer; one clean-cloth bearer; one gong-and-cymbal bearer; one water-jar bearer; one folding-chair bearer; and one axe bearer. When the emperor left the private chambers they stood divided outside the chamber gate, guiding him to the hall; when he ascended the throne they descended the steps to wait; only after he re-entered the chambers were the guards dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At regular audiences, hall sessions, suburban and temple rites, and imperial visits, whenever the palanquin moved there were close attendants: two with gilded silver maces; ten fan bearers; four whisk holders; two incense-box and two incense-ball bearers; two tally and two banner bearers; and one each for bowl, spittoon, clean cloth, gong and cymbals, water jar, folding chair, and axe. When the emperor left his private chambers they posted outside the gate and escorted him to the hall; when he took the throne they waited below the steps; only after he withdrew to the inner chambers were the guards dismissed.

translations.literal: Purple treasure-flower jackets, silver-brown forehead belts.
translations.idiomatic: Purple treasure-flower jackets and silver-brown forehead belts.

sentences.zh: 後部鼓吹三百三十七人：鼓吹丞二人，典士四人，部轄指揮使一人，主帥十八人，金鉦、掆鼓各三，羽葆鼓十二，歌二十四，拱辰管二十四，簫二十四，笳二十四，節鼓二，鐃鼓十二，歌十六，簫二十四，笳二十四，小橫吹一百二十。

translations.literal: Rear band, 337 men: two band assistant directors, four ritual attendants, one section commander, eighteen section commanders, three chime gongs and three carrying-drums each, twelve feathered-canopy drums, twenty-four singers, twenty-four Gongshen pipes, twenty-four flutes, twenty-four horns, two beat drums, twelve cymbal drums, sixteen singers, twenty-four flutes, twenty-four horns, one hundred twenty small transverse wind players.
translations.idiomatic: The rear band numbered 337 men: two band assistant directors, four ritual attendants, one section commander, eighteen section commanders, three chime gongs and three carrying-drums each, twelve feathered-canopy drums, twenty-four singers, twenty-four Gongshen pipes, twenty-four flutes, twenty-four horns, two beat drums, twelve cymbal drums, sixteen singers, twenty-four flutes, twenty-four horns, and one hundred twenty small transverse wind players.

sentences.zh: 青苣紋袍、抹額、抹帶，餘並與前同。

translations.literal: Green rush-pattern robes, forehead bands, forehead belts; the remainder all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Green rush-pattern robes with forehead bands and belts; all other attire as before.

sentences.zh: 金吾牙門旗第三門，牙門旗四，旗三人，監門校尉六人。

translations.literal: Golden Guard gate-banner third gate: four gate banners, three men per flag, six gate-watching commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Golden Guard gate-banner third gate: four gate banners, three men per flag, and six gate-watching commandants.

sentences.zh: 服、執同第一門。

translations.literal: Attire and equipment the same as the first gate.
translations.idiomatic: Attire and equipment matched the first gate.

sentences.zh: 黃麾後第一部二百七十二人，第二部二百七十二人，第三部二百七十二人，殿中侍御、衛大將軍、折沖都尉、龍頭竿以下名色，並如前三部。

translations.literal: Behind the yellow banner, first section 272 men, second section 272 men, third section 272 men; attendant censors, guard great generals, assault-resistance commandants, dragon-head poles and below—all titles and colors as in the three sections before.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the yellow banner, the first, second, and third sections each numbered 272 men; attendant censors, guard great generals, assault-resistance commandants, dragon-head poles, and all titles and colors below matched the three sections above.

sentences.zh: 第八節。

translations.literal: Eighth section.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth section.

sentences.zh: 中道，後部鼓吹第二，百二十人：笛二十四，簫二十四，篳篥二十四，笳二十四，桃皮篳篥二十四。

translations.literal: Central path, rear band second unit, 120 men: twenty-four flutes, twenty-four panpipes, twenty-four oboes, twenty-four horns, twenty-four peach-skin oboes.
translations.idiomatic: On the central path, the rear band's second unit numbered 120 men: twenty-four flutes, twenty-four panpipes, twenty-four oboes, twenty-four horns, and twenty-four peach-skin oboes.

sentences.zh: 服並如前。

translations.literal: Attire all as before.
translations.idiomatic: Attire all as before.

sentences.zh: 屬車八，牛二十四，駕士八十人。

translations.literal: Eight attendant carriages, twenty-four oxen, eighty carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Eight attendant carriages with twenty-four oxen and eighty carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 武牟、緋繡雲鶴大袖、銀褐抹帶、大口袴。

translations.literal: Martial caps, scarlet embroidered cloud-crane large-sleeved jackets, silver-brown forehead belts, baggy trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Martial caps, scarlet embroidered cloud-crane large-sleeved jackets, silver-brown forehead belts, and baggy trousers.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞車，赤馬二，駕士十五人。

translations.literal: Yellow battle-axe carriage, two red horses, fifteen carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow battle-axe carriage had two red horses and fifteen carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 武牟、緋對鵝大袖、銀褐抹帶、大口褥。

translations.literal: Martial caps, scarlet facing-goose large-sleeved jackets, silver-brown forehead belts, baggy padded trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Martial caps, scarlet facing-goose large-sleeved jackets, silver-brown forehead belts, and baggy trousers.

sentences.zh: 豹尾車，赤馬二，駕士十五人。

translations.literal: Leopard-tail carriage, two red horses, fifteen carriage attendants.
translations.idiomatic: The leopard-tail carriage had two red horses and fifteen carriage attendants.

sentences.zh: 武弁、緋立豹大袖、銀褐抹帶、大口袴。

translations.literal: Martial caps, scarlet standing-leopard large-sleeved jackets, silver-brown sash belts, and baggy trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants wore martial caps, scarlet large-sleeved jackets emblazoned with standing leopards, silver-brown sash belts, and baggy trousers.

sentences.zh: 玄武隊六十一人：金吾折沖都尉一人，平巾幘、紫辟邪袍、革帶、袴、螣蛇、橫刀、弓矢。

translations.literal: Black Tortoise detachment, sixty-one men: one Golden Crow assault-and-rescue commandant; flat-cap kerchief, purple demon-quelling robe, leather belt, trousers, brocade serpent belt, side sword, and bow and arrow.
translations.idiomatic: The Black Tortoise detachment numbered sixty-one men: one Golden Crow assault-and-rescue commandant in flat-cap kerchief, purple demon-quelling robe, leather belt, trousers, brocade serpent belt, side sword, and bow and arrow.

sentences.zh: 皞槊二，平巾幘、緋寶相花衫、革大帶。

translations.literal: Two white spears; flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet treasure-flower jackets, and leather great belts.
translations.idiomatic: Two white spears, with bearers in flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet treasure-flower jackets, and leather great belts.

sentences.zh: 仙童旗一、玄武旗一、螣蛇旗一、神龜旗一、旗五人，服、執如前例。

translations.literal: One Immortal Boy banner, one Black Tortoise banner, one Serpent banner, and one Divine Tortoise banner; five men per banner; attire and equipment as in the preceding precedent.
translations.idiomatic: One Immortal Boy banner, one Black Tortoise banner, one Serpent banner, and one Divine Tortoise banner, five men per banner, with attire and equipment as in the preceding precedent.

sentences.zh: 槊十九，弓矢十五，弩四。

translations.literal: Nineteen spears, fifteen bow-and-arrow sets, and four crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen spears, fifteen bow-and-arrow sets, and four crossbows.

sentences.zh: 平巾幘、緋寶相花衫、革帶、袴。

translations.literal: Flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet treasure-flower jackets, leather belts, and trousers.
translations.idiomatic: Flat-cap kerchiefs, scarlet treasure-flower jackets, leather belts, and trousers.

sentences.zh: 黃麾後第四部二百七十二人，第五部二百七十二人，第六部二百七十二人，攝官名數服色並如前第四、第五、第六部。

translations.literal: Behind the yellow banner, the fourth section had 272 men, the fifth 272, and the sixth 272; acting officers, names, numbers, and garment colors all matched the preceding fourth, fifth, and sixth sections.
translations.idiomatic: Behind the yellow banner, the fourth, fifth, and sixth sections numbered 272 men each; acting officers, titles, numbers, and uniform colors all followed the specifications given for the fourth, fifth, and sixth sections above.

sentences.zh: 絳引幡二十，執者六十人。

translations.literal: Twenty crimson guide pennants, sixty bearers.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty crimson guide pennants with sixty bearers.

sentences.zh: 並武弁、緋繡寶相花衫、銀褐抹帶、大口袴。

translations.literal: All in martial caps, scarlet embroidered treasure-flower jackets, silver-brown sash belts, and baggy trousers.
translations.idiomatic: All wore martial caps, scarlet embroidered treasure-flower jackets, silver-brown sash belts, and baggy trousers.

sentences.zh: 諸從駕官並於仗後陪從，朝服不足者公服。

translations.literal: All officials accompanying the imperial procession were to attend behind the armed guard; those who lacked court dress wore public dress.
translations.idiomatic: All officials accompanying the procession were to follow behind the armed guard; those without full court dress wore public dress instead.

sentences.zh: 凡應乘馬者，並同宋制。

translations.literal: As for all who were to ride horses, the regulations matched Song practice.
translations.idiomatic: All who were to ride horses followed Song regulations.
